capabilities.title: Pause keeps memory
capabilities.plain: Pausing keeps memory and running programs, so the machine resumes exactly where it was.

rows.shortfall: A sleep usually comes back where it left off, but a wake that has to rebuild starts fresh and loses what was running.
rows.note: Auto-sleep is off by default; a stop never keeps memory.

rows.shortfall: Network connections do not survive; only files and processes do.

source.quote: Memory state is maintained even after scaling down, including the running processes and entire filesystem.

rows.note: There is no pause; a stop removes the machine and keeps a copy of the disk.

source.quote: There is no pause. A stop removes the virtual machine and keeps a copy of the disk.

rows.shortfall: A hibernated machine wakes in about 85 ms; standby is faster still.

source.quote: Next to `running`, boxd has two sleep states: `standby` keeps the memory in RAM, and `hibernated` writes it to disk.

rows.note: There is no paused state; when an instance stops, its processes and its disk end with it.

source.quote: An instance runs only until something stops it, and its processes and the files on its disk end with it. The next `start()` creates a new instance.

rows.shortfall: Only the full virtual machine can be paused with memory; a container sandbox loses what was running.

source.quote: Pause is not supported for container sandboxes. The filesystem can be preserved on stop, but memory state is not.

rows.note: A filesystem-only pause is opt-in; the default keeps memory.

source.quote: By default a pause saves **both** the filesystem and the memory.

rows.shortfall: A resume can come back without the running programs, and the machine reports that it did.
rows.note: A paused machine cannot be stopped; start it first.

source.quote: **Resume** brings back a paused machine's memory and processes. If that is not possible it starts fresh: files are kept, processes are not.

rows.shortfall: A fast pause keeps only the files, so it is the option to avoid if work must survive.
